text: The model has identified features that it associates with glioma. Glioma is a broad term for tumours that arise from the glial cells of the central nervous system and can range from slowly growing lesions to aggressive high-grade tumours; the term alone does not convey type or grade, which are required for prognosis and management [nci-cns-pdq-hp] [who-cns5]. Imaging alone cannot determine grade or molecular subtype, and the classifier does not provide information on tumour margins or volume [nci-cns-pdq-hp]. Consequently this output should be understood as a classification, not a confirmed diagnosis. Clinical correlation is essential, and the finding should be discussed with a qualified neuro-oncology team, including neurosurgery, neuro-radiology and pathology, to consider further imaging, possible biopsy and molecular characterisation as per current WHO guidelines [who-cns5] [nci-cns-pdq-hp]. In India, referral to a multidisciplinary centre within the National Cancer Grid is the usual pathway for suspected glioma [ncg-india] [who-cns5]. Prompt assessment is advised if any neurological red-flag symptoms develop [ninds-brain-tumors].
